reason: The cited evidence shows that friction-induced oxide films can reduce wear (E1) and friction (E2) in other alloys, but neither passage involves Si doping, the CoCrFeMnNi system, or silica-based oxides. The specific claims about Si promoting a lubricious, adherent oxide over the stated temperature range and the quantitative improvement are unsupported by the provided references.
premises: Frictional heating in air can induce an oxide film on a multi-component alloy surface that reduces friction and wear.
A lubricious oxide film can form in situ during sliding contact without prior surface treatment.
Silicon doping in CoCrFeMnNi will promote a silica-based oxide that is lubricious and adherent.
The oxide film will remain continuous and effective from ~300 K to 900 K under ambient air.
A ~40% reduction in friction coefficient and significantly lower wear rate are achievable with 1–2 at.% Si.
